None appear. Every 'gold' is either 'gold tone' or a colour word for a part: 'gold claws' (K09, K10, K12), 'gold rim' (K08) and 'tiny gold beads' (K11). The beads follow the same house pattern as claws and rim. K12's 'Metal: Stainless steel' comes only from the printed supplier card, as the README says. Every size is worded as about or approximately. My spot checks on the photos agree with the measurement notes: K10 is about 122x152 px on a 1109 px card, so 8.8x11 mm. K13 has 4 bezels and 3 claw settings, centre claw-set, about 143 px pitch, so about 1 cm, and about 930 px along the curve, so about 6.5 cm. K12 is about 340x235 px at 15.7 px/mm, so about 22x15 mm.

summary: I found no blockers and nothing that needs fixing. All six drafts match ship_26nov_b2.json exactly (k08 to k13): title, handle, DRAFT status, vendor, productType, taxonomy category, tags, descriptionHtml byte for byte, SEO, SKU ADT37 to ADT42, price, unitCost, inventory (tracked, 10 at Location/76267389090), DENY policy, no compare-at, and all metafields, including ring-size 5 to 8 on the two rings. Prices are 3.5 x the price written on each supplier photo, rounded half up (155→543, 290→1015, 260→910, 320→1120, 290→1015, 300→1050), and cost equals that supplier price. The two rings each have one READY size-guide image. Both description image URLs return HTTP 200 to curl and match the local cards (mean difference about 0.3 of 255). The other four have no media. All six publications read autoPublish false. Each product sits on those six channels (count 6; V2 shows isPublished false) and none is published (published count 0, publishedAt null). Searches by handle, SKU and title find no duplicates. The copy contains no banned words or claims, and every named styling-tip product is ACTIVE. Notes for the owner: three of those tip products (Lumière Oval Solitaire Ring, Cushion Solitaire Ring, Teardrop Lariat) are sold out today. The recorded creation time of 09:40 UTC should read about 09:53 UTC. Ring range, closures and the necklace length remain open items, as the README says.
